source_excerpts.text:
CORRECTABLE PARITY METER
Assume P/Q block preservation, on-code H=J X_L+lambda Z_L X_a plus a common logical-independent bath generator, constant real J,lambda, and Q evolution preserving the measured ancilla Z. Arbitrary Q-confined hidden motion is allowed. Let omega=sqrt(J^2+lambda^2). One pulse gives K1=-i(lambda/omega)sin(omega*t)Z_L P tensor U_M; correcting Z_L leaves a scalar accepted action. Rejection can still consume an unknown input, and a zero success scalar is possible.
For lambda>=J>0 use opposite drive signs in two windows t1=alpha/omega, t2=(pi-alpha)/omega, with sin^2(alpha)=omega^2/(2lambda^2). Direct Pauli multiplication makes the on-code rejecting coefficient -1+2lambda^2*sin^2(alpha)/omega^2=0 and sin(omega*(t1+t2))=0. The accepted coefficient is i[(J/lambda)Y_L+sqrt(1-J^2/lambda^2)Z_L] tensor U_M, a known unitary up to phase. Q cannot accept under the stated ancilla-conservation premise; its rejecting memory evolution remains its actual Q dynamics, not automatically a Lüders identity. This reconstructs the two-window family from the acquired native formulas. The extra three-window family and producer11-study residuals are not newly audited without their missing detailed proof/code.

CONSERVED SYMMETRY AND AVAILABILITY
If full in-code U commutes with X_L Z_a, the <1_a|U|0_a> block anticommutes with X_L, hence has exactly Y_L tensor A_M+Z_L tensor B_M. Q also needs its stated ancilla-Z conservation to prevent off-code clicks. Strong bath modulation is allowed only if that complete symmetry holds; no such conservation is acquired by a gate endpoint calibration.
For a fresh Bell candidate, all four corrected Bell outcomes, and retired/coarsened Bell labels, Pauli-character orthogonality removes the Y/Z cross terms. After the known Z correction the accepted unnormalized task has I/X bath CP paths. A ZZ test distinguishes those paths. Trusted preparation/terminal/correction, reference frame, unknown-input holding and record retirement remain required. There is no additional Pauli-frame randomization under this explicitly coarse completed-task boundary.
In the bath interaction picture, let the coupling's initial minimum singular value be ell, its change rate <=kappa, and total bounded controlled interaction norm<=v. Duhamel gives first-order amplitude -it Lambda(0) and remainder <=(kappa+v^2)t^2/2. Reverse triangle gives success >=[ell*t-(kappa+v^2)t^2/2]_+^2. Applying a uniform history-conditional lower bound to each fresh candidate gives rejection tail <=(1-s0)^n without a bath reset. It does not follow from a bare coupling gap alone: Omega X with coupling Z gives sin^2(t sqrt(Omega^2+1))/(Omega^2+1), tending to zero. The reported240 trajectories and numerical confidence examples remain source reports.

source_excerpts.text:
TELEPORTATION FINE-RECORD COUNTEREXAMPLE
The coarse boundary is essential, not a stylistic qualification. After the known correction take the accepted Bell-resource operator K=(I+X)/2, obtainable from a Y/Z branch before correction. Corrected Bell outcome m has operator P_m K P_m/2=(I+chi_m X)/4. For input|+>, the two chi=+ outcomes each have probability1/4 and the other two probability0; for|-> these labels reverse. Total acceptance is1/2 for both. Summing the Bell labels gives (rho+X rho X)/4, the intended positive I/X paths. Keeping the fine label gives input-dependent outcome probabilities, which cannot be represented by I/X errors with bath-only coefficients independent of the unknown input. The old U1023 fine-record obstruction remains valid. This review does not accept a flagged-instrument equality across that changed boundary.
